title: Localization of the actual kernel conormal and unit
statement: Let g:X→Y be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], W⊂Y and U⊂X opens with g⁻¹W=U and h:U⊆g⁻¹W. Suppose i=g.resLE W U h:U→W is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let K=ker(O_Y→g_*O_X) be the actual module-sheaf kernel and N=P_g K [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let C=i_*P_i(i.ker.toModules), using the closed-immersion ideal module [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Give Γ(N,U) the Γ(W,top)-action through the open-section isomorphism W.topIso.hom and g.appLE. There exists a Γ(W,top)-linear equivalence e:Γ(C,top)≃Γ(N,U). For every s∈Γ(K,W), there is t∈Γ(i.ker.toModules,top) whose inclusion is W.topIso.inv of the included s, and e carries the local pullback-unit section of t to the restriction to U of the original pullback-unit section of s [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. No assumption that g is globally closed is made.

source.place: Tag 01R3 (1), (2), combined with Tags 00A0 and 0096; read online 2026-10-13

proof.text: The preimage equality and the defining commutative square of resLE identify i with the restriction of g to W. On every open T in W, the open-section isomorphisms identify O_Y→g_*O_X with O_W→i_*O_U. Restriction preserves the actual kernel: evaluation on an open is left exact, and the open-section identifications commute with both structure maps. The closed-immersion ideal module is this kernel, yielding the unique ideal section t with the asserted inclusion equation.

Use tensor-pullback composition around the commutative square of open inclusions to transport the kernel identification to its pullback. For the open inclusions, pullback is restriction. The composition isomorphisms are those supplied by uniqueness of left adjoints to the same pushforward.

Choose the composition and restriction isomorphisms by the unit compatibility of uniqueness of left adjoints. The canonical unit of exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction is the sheafification of 1 tensor the inverse-image unit; restriction changes neither the sectionwise tensor nor its sheafification unit. Thus the local unit of t corresponds to the restricted original unit of s. Take top sections and the open-section identifications to produce e; both scalar structures are through g.appLE composed with W.topIso.hom.
